title: Building a message
idea: Join string variables and little bits of text to build a full sentence.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

name = "Mia"
print("Hello, " + name)
exercises.explanation: The fixed text "Hello, " (with its space) joins the value of name: Hello, Mia.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

name = "Mia"
print("Hi " + name + "!")
exercises.explanation: Three pieces joined: "Hi ", the name, and "!". The space lives inside "Hi ".

exercises.prompt: You can mix fixed text and variables in the same join to build a sentence.
exercises.explanation: That's the whole point. "Welcome, " + name + "!" mixes text you type with text you stored.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

city = "Hanoi"
print("I live in " + city)
exercises.explanation: "I live in " ends with a space, then the value of city joins on: I live in Hanoi.

exercises.prompt:
Arrange these pieces to print the message: Dear Sam,

The pieces are joined left to right with +.
exercises.explanation: "Dear " + name + "," builds Dear Sam, when name holds "Sam".

exercises.prompt:
Finish the line so it prints: Bye, Mia

name = "Mia"
print("Bye, " + ____)
exercises.explanation: No quotes! We want the value stored in name, so we write the bare variable name.

options: name is in quotes, so it shows the word name, not Mia
exercises.explanation: Quotes around name make it the literal text 'name'. Drop the quotes to use the variable's value.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that prints: Welcome, Mia (name holds "Mia").
exercises.explanation: The text "Welcome, " (with a trailing space) joins the value of name: Welcome, Mia.

exercises.prompt:
What will this show?

pet = "dog"
sound = "woof"
print("The " + pet + " says " + sound)
exercises.explanation: Four pieces joined with spaces tucked into the text parts: The dog says woof.

exercises.prompt: Building messages by + works, but it is easy to forget a space or a quote.
exercises.explanation: It works, but it's fiddly. Next lesson shows a cleaner way: f-strings.
